Subject: Post-call recap: LumenWave deployment SLOs & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — good discussion. Quick written recap so we all have the same set of asks and next steps.

Key pain points (as we heard):
- 95th/99th token-level latency spikes during batch ingestion windows (current API 95p ~ 420ms).
- Periods of burst traffic (up to ~150 req/s sustained for short windows) causing KV cache misses and higher per-token cost.
- Regulatory requirement: per-customer retention controls and audit logs for model inputs/outputs.

Primary goals you shared:
1) Reduce tail latency to <= 200ms token 95p for interactive features; 99p target ~ 350ms.
2) Support steady-state throughput of 80–120 req/s with headroom for 200 req/s bursts.
3) Keep unit inference cost within a 1.7–2.2x multiple of current on-prem spend.
4) Retain customer-level logs for 90 days behind customer-specific encryption keys.

Technical constraints noted:
- Model: evaluating two families — a 30B dense model for quality and a 7B quantized variant for high-throughput endpoints. Typical sequence length ~ 512 tokens, peak 2k during long-context experiments.
- KV cache hit rate today is low (~12%) because prompts vary across customers; caching strategy will be important.
- Network egress to Azure region east-us is a preference for lowest latency to your infra.

Redwood's initial recommendations (high level):
- Hosting: start on Dedicated pools in us-east with canary traffic on Hosted API. Dedicated gives predictable capacity for 120 req/s and deterministic latency.
- KV caching: enable per-tenant prefix caching + a small shared prefix cache; we’ll run a short cache-sensitivity test during the next workshop.
- Model variants: serve a 30B model for high-quality routes and a quantized 7B for low-latency paths; automatic routing by policy (latency vs cost).
- Quantization & batching: we recommend int8 quantization for the 7B route and adaptive batching with a 20ms max-delay threshold to keep p95 latency stable.

Action items / owners:
- Redwood (Logan): share post-call deck + initial KV cache sizing worksheet (attached). Due: end of day 8/3.
- Redwood (Karthik): produce initial topology options (hosted/dedicated/private) with queueing models and cost estimates. Due: EOD 8/4.
- LumenWave (Elena): share sample traffic profile (1 week preferred) and compliance contact for KMS/HSM questions. Due: 8/6.
- LumenWave (Rajiv): confirm regulatory encryption/backups requirements and procurement timeline. Due: 8/10.

Next steps:
- Technical workshop with SEs + infra engineers (60–90 min) — propose Thu 8/5 10:00–11:30 PT.
- Procurement/contract discussion scheduled the following week once we lock topology cost ranges.

Attachments: LW-postcall-deck.pdf (high-level recap), kv-cache-proposal.xlsx (worksheet).

Thanks — I’ll update the HubSpot record and share the Drive folder shortly.

Elena / Rajiv — adding a bit more technical detail ahead of the Thu workshop. I’ll bring a short slide with queuing/capacity math but wanted to surface the topology options and a few questions we should prioritize.

Topology options (pros/cons):
1) Dedicated pools (us-east) — recommended start
   - Pros: deterministic latency, reserved GPU capacity for 30B routes, easier SLO guarantees.
   - Cons: higher baseline cost, slower to scale for unexpected multi-tenant bursts (we can configure short burst capacity).

2) Hosted API + Dedicated hybrid
   - Pros: can route overflow/bursts to Hosted for elasticity; lower committed cost.
   - Cons: slightly higher variance in tail latency during failover; must test fallback routing and model parity.

3) Private VPC on your cloud (east-us)
   - Pros: full control on networking and KMS; best for strict compliance.
   - Cons: longer deployment lead time and heavier ops for you.

Model & serving notes:
- Candidate models: 30B dense (baseline) and 7B int8 quantized (low-latency). We should run a perf matrix: p50/p95/p99 for sequence lengths 128/512/2048.
- Batching: target adaptive batching with a 20ms max-wait cap for interactive endpoints; for bulk inference windows we can switch to larger batches.
- KV cache: per-tenant prefix cache + shared LRU for common system prompts. We should run a 48-hour cache-hit experiment to estimate real savings; template attached in kv-cache-proposal.xlsx.
- Networking: recommend colocating Dedicated pool in east-us3 (closest to your Azure egress) to minimize RTT.

Questions for the workshop (please confirm in advance):
- Can you share a 48-hour sample of request sizes and inter-arrival times (we need timestamps + seq_len + route id)?
- Which customers require per-customer KMS keys vs team-level keys? (this affects key management flow)
- Are long-context (2k tokens) requests tolerant of higher latency if we route them separately?

I'll prepare two cost bands (conservative / optimized) and a deployment timeline to present on Thu.
